name: IEC JK flip-flop (rectangular form)
summary: IEC bistable with 1J and 1K inputs controlled by a dynamic C1 clock; J=K=1 toggles the state.
description: The IEC JK flip-flop has inputs labelled 1J and 1K, both controlled by C1. On the active clock transition J=1, K=0 sets; J=0, K=1 resets; J=K=1 toggles; and J=K=0 holds. A negation mark outside the C1 input with the wedge indicates a falling-edge device.

JK devices are used in counters and divider chains. On IEC drawings check the clock marking carefully, because rising-edge and falling-edge versions are visually similar and mixing them changes counter sequencing.
The rectangle does not reveal whether the device is edge-triggered or pulse-triggered unless the clock and output marks are read together. A postponed output mark indicates a pulse-triggered type.
readingNotes: Read the clock edge from the wedge and any external negation.
drawingChecklist: Label J and K with the C prefix.
Show the active clock edge clearly.
Show asynchronous S and R inputs where present.
distinction: An IEC T flip-flop has a single 1T input; a JK with J and K tied high behaves the same way.
